findings.title: TD-7's example recommendation strings contradict the `review`/`blocked` stable-vocabulary contract the arch commits to runners
findings.description: The arch (240-arch §Related Work, Amoeba) requires "a stable vocabulary" of new `recommendation` string values, and gives literal examples: `{ recommendation: "review", ... }` and `{ recommendation: "blocked", ... }`. The slice's own Overview, Value and "Provides to Other Slices" repeat that **`review` / `blocked`** are "the stable strings runners route on," and TD-3 says the branch "maps `pending-review` → `review` and `review-failed` → `blocked`." But TD-7's concrete examples emit prose sentences as the `recommendation` value — `'Review required before advancing'` and `'Blocked: review verdict does not clear threshold'` — and then close with "Exact strings finalized in implementation." Prose containing variable content is not a routeable token, and keying a runner on a user-visible label is explicitly forbidden by the project's own rule against user-accessible labels as logical structure. As written the design contains two mutually exclusive contracts, so the implementer cannot know which one 242/243 and Amoeba will code against. Fix: declare `recommendation` to be the literal tokens `review` / `blocked` (from a named constant, per the no-magic-strings rule the design already invokes), and move the prose to `rationale`/`summary`, which is where TD-7's own text says the review type, verdict and threshold belong.

findings.title: The position-derived model silently drops the arch's per-boundary opt-out, and the arch's own text is unreconciled
findings.description: The arch's Design Goal "**Config-driven**" states that "which transitions require a review, which reviewType satisfies each … are all configurable per project without a code change," and its per-transition `review_gates` table is the mechanism that expresses *which* boundaries are gated. Under TD-4 + TD-1, all four boundaries always owe exactly one review whenever `review_enabled = true`: `review_type` is inert, and there is no per-boundary on/off. There is also no value that disables a boundary — `threshold` is enum-constrained to `pass`/`concerns`, and `PASS` clears under both — so a team wanting code reviews but *not* task-breakdown reviews cannot express it, and adding or suppressing a boundary now requires a code change in `BOUNDARY_REVIEW_TYPE`. Separately, the arch's Scope and §"Initiative-level gating (v1 deferred)" say "v1 implements only the four slice-level transitions" and assign the `pre-slice-plan` gate to a later slice; 241 folds it in on the plan's Phase-4 authority (240-slices Notes), but the design cites only the plan/PM and never acknowledges contradicting the arch text. Requirement left unmet: a user-visible way to gate a subset of boundaries, and traceability between the design and two now-stale arch statements. Fix: name the per-boundary opt-out as an explicit gap (a `review_gates.{boundary}.enabled` style key is the lightest option, or an empty/inert override) and record it in the initiative's Future Work, and add one line to the design stating that it supersedes the arch's "v1 slice-level only" and "configurable which-review" language so an implementer reading the arch does not treat pre-slice-plan gating as out of scope.

findings.title: No failure mode enumerated for config reads on the new I/O path, and it lands inside an error path that collapses to a benign status
findings.description: The design adds `this.config?.get(...)` calls into `deriveSliceStatus()` (TD-3) but never enumerates what happens when a config read throws. `ConfigManager.get()` throws for an unknown key and re-throws any non-ENOENT read/parse error, so a malformed or permission-blocked `.context-forge.toml` is an exception, not a default. Two consequences the design must pick between and state: (1) if the exception propagates, `cf next` / `cf status` / `workflow_next` / `workflow_status` gain a new hard failure mode for projects where gating is *off* — directly contradicting the success criterion "output is identical to pre-241 for every project" and adding config-file I/O to a path that previously read none; (2) if it is swallowed, it is swallowed by an existing broad catch in `deriveSliceStatus()` whose current behavior is to return the base `no-active-slice` status, which then routes to the no-active-slice guard and produces first-run guidance such as "Create architecture document" — a silently wrong recommendation, against both the project's no-silent-fallback rule and the arch's "Gate is a routing rule, not a decision." Requirement left unmet: an explicit handling strategy for config-read failure per boundary. Fix: specify that gate evaluation is excluded from the existing collapse path, and that a config read failure surfaces as an explicit error/rationale (or a named third outcome distinct from `pending`/`failed`), plus a test for a malformed config.

findings.title: Invalid/unrecognized config token values are unspecified at gate-read time; the arch requires fail-fast, not silent pass or silent block
findings.description: `resolveGateConfig()` "reads `review_enabled` + `review_threshold` + `review_unknown_as`" and the patterns section says to "narrow explicitly," but the design defines no outcome for a token that is present yet not in the declared `ThresholdToken`/`UnknownPolicy` unions. `ConfigManager` validates only on `set()` — `get()` returns the raw TOML leaf unvalidated — so a hand-edited `workflow.review_threshold = "bogus"` or `workflow.review_gates.pre_advance.threshold = "passs"` reaches the gate. The arch's "Fail-fast on configuration errors" principle names this exact case ("An invalid `workflow.review_threshold` value or an unrecognized per-gate config is a config error surfaced immediately, not a silent pass or silent block"). The design's types make an accidental silent default easy: the decision matrix has a row for every `Verdict` but no branch for a bad threshold, so a `switch` without a default either fails to be exhaustive or quietly falls through. Also unstated: an unrecognized per-gate transition name, which TD-4 says 241 "consumes" for threshold only. Fix: add the explicit invalid-token outcome (recommend: gate does not evaluate; surface an error/rational naming the key and the offending value) to TD-1/TD-2, and add it to the test matrix in "Technical Requirements."

findings.title: Path resolution from detector output to the parser is unstated, and the never-throw parser makes a wrong path indistinguishable from a missing verdict
findings.description: The data flow pipes `detectDocuments(projectPath, index, 'code').review` straight into `parseFrontmatter(path)`. The `review` slot holds a **project-relative** path, while `parseFrontmatter` performs a filesystem `readFile`, so a `join(projectPath, …)` step is required — a step the design's own sibling handling of task paths already performs but which this flow diagram omits. The gap is amplified by the property the design explicitly relies on ("This parser never throws — it returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` … exactly the behavior the gate needs"): an unresolvable path returns the identical shape to "file present, no `verdict` field," so a resolution bug is *undetectable at the gate* and, with the default `review_unknown_as = fail`, would report `review-failed` for every gated slice including ones with a clean `PASS` review. Requirement left unmet: the arch's file-read failure-mode rule that "the rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly" — impossible if existence, unreadability, and absent-verdict all collapse to one signal. Fix: state the path-join contract, and require a presence check (or a distinguishable "resolved path unreadable" outcome) so that *absent*, *present-unparseable*, and *present-no-verdict* remain three separable cases as TD-2 already insists `pending` vs `failed` must be.

findings.title: Whether a gated status replaces or augments the lifecycle status is unspecified, and replacement loses the boundary position from every status consumer
findings.description: TD-3 makes status derivation the single source of truth, so `slice` and `tasks` gates fire at the `needs-tasks` and `in-implementation` boundaries and the review-gate branch "only routes." `SliceStatus.status` is a single scalar union, so setting `pending-review`/`review-failed` there necessarily *overwrites* `needs-tasks`/`in-implementation` (the branches at those positions test `slice.status === …` and would no longer match). The design never says this, and the consequences are unhandled: the summary line and `workflow_status` consumers see "slice NNN pending-review" with no indication of *which* boundary is blocked or how far the slice actually got (e.g. design present, no task file), and `NextAction`'s `phase` field for these states is undefined in TD-7, where the existing sibling branches all set it. It also changes a documented MCP response value set without listing the addition (243 covers prose docs, not the tool's own response-shape enumeration). Requirement left unmet: "First-class status representation … runners can act on them" — a runner cannot act correctly on a status that silently erases the work position. Fix: state the choice explicitly — either keep the lifecycle status and carry the gate outcome in an added field, or set the gate status and include the blocked boundary + phase in `SliceStatus`/`NextAction` — and add the new enum values to the tool's documented status list.

findings.title: The `code` boundary's trigger value is typed by a different union than `STATUS`, so "define once" is not achieved for the gate's own key
findings.description: TD-6 correctly reproduces `NormalizedStatus` from `STATUS` byte-identically, and the ~50-site sweep is properly assigned to 910 rather than smuggled in here. One residual: the gate's trigger is `inferredStatus === STATUS.Complete`, but that field's declared type is its own inline union (`complete`/`in-progress`/`not-started`), not `NormalizedStatus`. The values coincide today, so behavior is unaffected; a future rename would still require editing two definitions. Worth one line in the design (or in 910's scope note) stating whether the task-level union is narrowed to `NormalizedStatus` or a companion constant is introduced.

findings.title: No architecture NFR applies to this slice's path
findings.description: I searched the arch for latency/throughput/performance/NFR targets on the `getNext`/`workflow_next` path and found none, so the "restate the NFR with a specific target" rule does not bind this design and no finding is raised on that axis. Noted only so the absence is not read as an omission: the one cross-cutting property the arch *does* state is behavioral ("Projects that do not enable review gating see identical behavior to today"), and the design correctly operationalizes it as the gating-off regression test rather than by inspection.
